chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who came to his wife while she was menstruating. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should seek forgiveness of Allah and not repeat it.' I said: 'So upon him is the disciplining (adab)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, twenty-five lashes, a quarter of the penalty (hadd) of the adulterer, and he is belittled (saghir), because he came for unlawful intercourse (sifah).'

key_terms.أَدَبٌ: Disciplining or corporal punishment (lesser than hadd)
key_terms.حَدِّ الزَّانِي: The fixed penalty for an adulterer
key_terms.صَاغِرٌ: Belittled or held in low esteem (a legal status)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a man who has intercourse with his wife during menstruation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific legal penalty (adab) for conjugal intercourse during menstruation, prescribing twenty-five lashes as a quarter of the adulterer's hadd to signify its lesser severity compared to fornication. The ruling emphasizes both spiritual repentance (istighfar) and physical discipline, reflecting the Shia juristic view that this act is a sin requiring expiation but not the full hadd penalty. The designation of 'saghir' (belittled/humbled) underscores the moral gravity of engaging in sexual relations during a state of ritual impurity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl Al Hasimy who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a man who came to his wife and she was in menstruation. Heasws said: ‘He should seek Forgiveness of Allahazwj, and should not repeat it’. I said, ‘So upon him would be the disciplining?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, twenty five lashes, being a quarter of the Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer, and he would be belittled, because he came unlawfully’.
